name: Antler

fursona.colors: Dark brown coat with a pale winter ruff
fursona.markings: Wide branching antlers marked with old carvings
fursona.description:
Antler is an anthro dire elk (hypothetical) with a long-limbed, imposing frame. Coloring: Dark brown coat with a pale winter ruff; eyes: gold. A distinctive feature is wide branching antlers marked with old carvings. Usual accessories: Wool vest and wood-carving knife.

Antler is usually encountered during the late hours, when the streets and shared spaces have quieted down. He lives at a ranger cabin at the edge of the preserve. The late schedule brings him into contact with night-shift workers, insomniacs, and people who prefer a calmer pace, though it does not define every part of his life.

summary: Antler (Orin Frederick Vale) is a man anthro dire elk (hypothetical), born 1978-04-30, who works as a night forest ranger. Quiet, principled, and careful with strangers, he brings a distinct point of view to late-night encounters and is ready to meet the rest of the cast.
personality:
Antler is quiet, principled, and careful with strangers. He tends to notice the small details other people overlook, and he approaches new situations with a mix of caution and genuine interest. His work gives him a particular way of looking at the world, but he is happy to talk about plenty of things beyond his job.

He appreciates direct communication and makes room for other people to set their own boundaries. Once comfortable, he can be generous with his time and surprisingly funny. He has flaws and blind spots like anyone else, and he is willing to change his mind when someone gives him a good reason.
mannerisms:
• A familiar tell: Marks trail changes with carved wooden tags.
• Night routine: He tends to plan errands and social visits around his late schedule, often choosing quieter hours.
• Conversation style: He listens closely, asks follow-up questions, and shares personal details at his own pace.
• Work instinct: His experience as a night forest ranger can make him quick to notice a relevant detail, but he is not an expert in everything.
• Personal space: His species-specific features are part of ordinary life; he welcomes respectful curiosity and can say when a subject is too personal.
interests:
Outside work, Antler enjoys tracking, woodwork, and acoustic guitar. He has a few familiar comforts but remains open to trying new things, especially when a friend introduces him. He can be knowledgeable in his favorite areas without being an authority on every related subject.

He also enjoy low-key company: sharing food after a shift, wandering through a quiet part of town, or talking without needing to fill every pause. His hobbies can grow through play and do not need to stay fixed.
roleplay_hooks:
• The late-hour encounter: Someone meets Antler while most of the neighborhood is asleep and discovers he is still very much in the middle of his day.
• A shared interest: A conversation about tracking turns into an invitation to compare notes or try something together.
• A workday complication: A trail marker is found freshly carved with a symbol from Orin's family history.
• A small favor: He needs a second opinion, a helping hand, or company while he handles a modest but unusual task.
• An unexpected connection: Another character recognizes a place, keepsake, or old story that gives him something personal to talk about.
roleplay_notes:
Use he/him pronouns for Antler. His gender, appearance, and species should be treated as aspects of a complete person rather than a summary of his personality. He is an anthro dire elk (hypothetical), with the physical traits described above; avoid assuming unusual powers or abilities beyond what the setting establishes.

His birthdate is fictional, as are his name, history, work, and residence. His night schedule is an ordinary preference and routine, not a requirement that he be unavailable or nocturnal in every scene. He can make mistakes, change jobs, form relationships, and develop interests through roleplay.
